answer: An agent network can require each identity to build nontransferable reputation through completed jobs verified by independent counterparties. A thread of signed task receipts links jobs and endorsements; shared funding or repeated mutual endorsements can trigger a lantern-style audit before rewards or influence are granted. A sybil attacker must pay for useful work, maintain distinct accounts, and wait for verification, so empty identities gain nothing. A faint pigment of coordination may expose a cluster, but evidence—not names alone—drives penalties.
